column1: # THE aarch64 INTER MEMORY REGRESSION, ATTRIBUTED PER COMMIT ON BOTH ISAs AND FIXED.
# per-commit binaries, one binary per commit of 940b855a..a1a32ca2f built at that sha) and rust/tools/mem_peak.sh.
# grid: content=gradient qp=40 preset=13 8-bit 4:2:0, inter arm (2 frames, low-delay P, SVTAV1_FRAME_SHIFT=3).
# mac    = Apple M4 Pro, aarch64-apple-darwin, 16 KiB pages, libmalloc; /usr/bin/time -l max RSS (KiB), 7 rounds.
# r7900x = x86_64-linux; /usr/bin/time -v max RSS (KiB), 5 rounds; heaptrack peak heap (LIVE bytes, MB, one run).
# A refused encode is excluded by the harness (refused column was 0 for every row below).
# 1. PER-COMMIT SERIES (main's linear order). x86 columns are tight (spread < 1 %); mac medians are
#    threads=auto and carry the 8-15 % upward run-to-run spread perf-status.md records, so the mac MIN
#    is the statistic to read there.
# 2. A/B OF THE FIX (cand1 = a1a32ca2f + refresh-by-value + Arc-held LAST reference), INTERLEAVED, same session.
# 4. THE C ORACLE, same session (Bin/Release/libSvtAv1Enc.a unchanged; NOT rebuilt)
# 5. RATIOS port/C on the two inter cells
# 6. vmmap -summary AT THE PEAK SAMPLE, mac, threads=1, 2048 inter (resident MiB; "empty" = regions with
#    no live block that libmalloc still holds resident). C's peak sample: LARGE 98.1, SMALL 14.0, no empties.
# 7. CANONICAL tools/mem_peak.sh RUN ON THE CANDIDATE TREE, mac, both sides, 3 arms, MEDIAN OF 5 [min,max].
#    benchmarks/mem_aarch64_2026-09-03.tsv "after" (2048), same harness, same C library.
# * C's 1280 inter median landed on its upper mode this run (min 53008 = the flat value every other run
#   reads); against 52992 (§4) the cand1 ratio is 1.045. Read the §2 A/B for the inter cells.
